Always check if a=0 (then it's linear). This systematic approach works for all quadratics.

To find stationary points: 1) Differentiate f(x) to get f'(x). 2) Set f'(x)=0 and solve for x values—these are critical points. 3) For each critical point x₀, compute second derivative f''(x₀). 4) If f''(x₀)>0, it's a local minimum. 5) If f''(x₀)<0, it's a local maximum. 6) If f''(x₀)=0, use higher-order tests or analyze sign changes of f'(x) around x₀. 7) Optional: compute y=f(x₀) for coordinates.
